question: A mass on a spring, a guitar string, and an air column all vibrate approximately sinusoidally for small displacements, even though they are physically very different systems. Why does the linear restoring force F = -kx describe all of them?

answers.text: Any smooth potential energy curve looks approximately quadratic near a stable equilibrium, so the restoring force is approximately linear for small displacements.
All of these systems are secretly made of springs.
Linear forces are the only kind of force that exists in nature.
Small displacements eliminate all friction in the system.
